title: Tarawera Ultra-Trail by UTMB — TMiler race page (13-14 February 2027)
claims: The 2027 Tarawera Ultra-Trail by UTMB runs on 13-14 February 2027; the TMiler starts from Te Puia, Rotorua at 04:00 on Saturday 13 February, covers 163 km with 3,800 m of positive gain, has a maximum allowed time of 36 hours and an entry price of NZ$1,090.
The TMiler is described as a loop course that starts and finishes in Rotorua, takes in 8 lakes and runs beneath the maunga of Tarawera, Ruawahia and Wahanga.

The listed highlights are running along eight different lakes, the solitude of the Tarawera Forest, a boat ride across Lake Rotomahana, the waterfall on the Tarawera Falls track, the archaeological site of Buried Village, the towering redwoods, steam alongside the trail at Sulphur Point and a finish at the Village Green in downtown Rotorua.
The terrain consists of mostly single track trails, wide trails, forestry and sealed roads, and the page states that the courses are subject to change.

The aid-station table lists 16 rows from Te Puia (0 km) to Village Green (163.0 km), with distance from start, distance from the last aid station, distance to the next aid station, distance to the finish, cut-off time, spectator access, drop bags, timing point and available services.
The TMiler has 13 aid stations and 1 water point along its route.
Support crews can assist only at the aid stations indicated with spectator access, including 200 m either side of the aid station on course.
Pacers may join from Okataina onwards, must register online no later than 10 February 2027, may be two in number but only one at a time, and there are no pacers for T14, T21, T50 or T102.

TMiler drop bags are available at Buried Village 29.9 km, Rerewhakaaitu 56.0 km, Outlet 88.8 km, Okataina 118.5 km, Tikitapu (Blue Lake) 145.7 km and Village Green 162.7 km, and must be dropped at Athlete Check-In before 8:00pm Friday.
The page states: 'The TMiler is a UTMB Worlds Series 100M Event. Finishers of TMiler will receive 4 running stones.'
The page lists the first finisher at 14 hr 53 min (6:53pm), the final finisher at 36 hr 00 min (4:07pm Sunday) and a required cut-off pace of 13:17 min/km.
Some sections of the course are publicly accessible for training, but the entire Tarawera Forest is private land and out of bounds to all athletes outside race day.
TMiler athletes must have their mandatory gear checked before they can collect their race pack.

Cut-off times are calculated from the departure time of the last athlete crossing the start timing point, athletes must leave the designated checkpoint before the advertised cut-off time, and if a runner cannot reach a checkpoint cut-off or finish within the total allowable time the organiser may classify the runner as a DNF and ask them to leave the course.
The minimum age for the race is 18 years on race day.
The event homepage states: 'Tarawera Ultra-Trail by UTMB is New Zealand's Premier trail running event held in Rotorua, New Zealand's birthplace of tourism.'
The TMiler race page states: 'The TMiler is one of the most scenic 100 mile runs in the world.'
